product_title: Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life
review_text:
Yummy freeze dried strawberries! I first had freeze dried strawberries years ago in the Special K red cereal and while the cereal, overall, sucked, I became mildly obsessed with the dried strawberries and would buy boxes just to pick out the strawberries.

I began buying the Nutri Store Freeze Dried strawberries fairly recently and enjoyed them. I bought this pair of #10 cans discounted to review, knowing I would receive another quality product.

Freeze dried fruit is pretty expensive, as it takes so many dehydrated strawberries to fill a container, but they last for a long time and can be used in so many ways. I typically eat them as a hard candy, just letting them kind of dissolve in my mouth, to get my sugar fix. I also add them to smoothies and shakes, rather than buying the pricier prepared flavor shake mixes. I have also used these strawberries in pancakes, muffins and dessert breads. So versatile and the cans stretch a long way.

The flavor and texture of the Nutristore berries is excellent. Not rock hard, brittle or chewy and gummy. Every can I Have used has been filled with full slices, very little broken pieces or "strawberry dust".

An excellent value for the quality received!

product_title: Hammer Recoverite Recovery Drink (Pack of 6), Subtle Citrus
review_text:
As a long-distance competitive runner, our college-athlete son undergoes weekly training mileage of 100-120 miles a week as preparation for the various races he's gearing up for. With this level of strenuous exercise, he understands the importance of the recovery period immediately following in which the body rebuilds itself even more fit than before. An intake of appropriate and bio-available protein with a good mix of complex carbohydrates within an hour or two after a strenuous workout is important in maintaining/repairing lean muscle mass.

Recoverite provides your body with the appropriate 3:1 ratio of complex carbohydrates and whey protein, along with the amino acid glutamine, the antioxidant l-carnosine, and a full balance of electrolytes. The benefits of all these ingredients are better and faster recovery by minimizing muscle soreness, rebuilding muscle tissue, as well as restoring the depleted glycogen in the muscles. The glutamine in the mix plays an important role in the health of the digestive tract and strengthening of the body's immune system.

This Hammer Recoverite in the chocolate flavor has worked out very well for him. It mixes easily with just milk or water; or sometimes he'll add a frozen banana and ice in the blender to make a smoothie when he has more time. Some protein mixes have made him nauseous when consumed immediately after an extreme workout. This Recoverite drink digests easily and gives him no stomach distress or cramping. I like the fact that it's made with all natural ingredients and contains no artificial sweeteners, gluten, or MSG.

For serious endurance athletes, this recovery drink is a great choice for bouncing back from strenuous workouts...allowing the athlete to accomplish more in their training regimen. As a reminder...this Recoverite is not the type of protein powder drink used by body builders. Instead, it works to maintain/build lean muscle.

For those people who like to know all the ingredients in the products they consume, the ingredient listing on the chocolate flavor is: Maltodextrin, Whey Protein Isolate, L-Glutamine, Cocoa, Natural Flavor, Calcium Chelate, Xylitol, Magnesium Chelate, Stevia, Potassium Chelate, L-Carnosine, Glycine, Salt, L-Tyrosine, Manganese Chelate, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Chromium Polynicotinate.

product_title: Wise Foods Gluten Free Freeze Dried Fruit 156 Servings
review_text:
I eat this stuff dry right out of the bag. I'm on a low-cal diet with 0 processed sugars and this stuff is addictive like candy. I ate this entire pail of fruit within 3 days of receiving it. Kinda stupid really, considering I could have bought the equivalent in fresh fruit at a fraction of the cost. Dat convenience and space saving though!!

Taste is what you'd expect from any freeze dried food eaten w/o hydration. Heavy cardboard top notes with a welcome and pleasant floral/fruity finish. I would rank the taste/mouth experience from best to worst as Banana-Peach-Strawberry-Apple. The Banana was especially addictive due to it's larger size and formidable crunch... An excellent potato chip alternative. The strawberry tasted as though they were made from unripened fruit, somewhat acidic/sour and not sweet. The peach tasted fine. The apple was too bland with a typical tangy apple finish that just didn't linger for long.

Yeah, I know It's pretty stupid of me to go through so much in so little time, but I'm a 6'4" 300lb monster and my diet up till then was so boring and bland that this stuff was a welcome change.

Would I buy it again? No, just the banana perhaps, but definitely not the rest.
pain_point: Some freeze dried fruits (strawberry, apple) have less desirable taste

product_title: Datrex 3600 Emergency Food Bar - 3 Day/72 Hour Bar - Single Pack
review_text:
Here is a quick review of the Datrex emergency ration kit. When most people talk about survival or put themselves in a mock survival situation, they talk about shelter, fire, water, and food. People tend to think about food last because they typically claim they are going to set a few snares and catch wild game. This mindset is impractical and usually considered by those who have limited hunting experience and likely no trapping experience. The fact is, it is not easy to snare small game.

Anyway, This kit is issued by the US Coastguard and included on on their lifeboats. This kit is designed to feed a person for three days. This kit contains 18 bars that are individually wrapped. There is a total of 3600 calories per pack, or 200 calories per bar. There is also 2.8 grams of protein per bar. Datrex also sells another style in a white package that contains 2400 calories. These rations are designed to not induce thirst, which is good in case you are in a situation in which you have limited access to water (such as a lifeboat situation). This pack weighs 1 pound 6 oz and has a five year shelf life. The taste is similar to that of a coconut cookie, without the raw coconut texture. If opened properly, the package itself can serve as a water container. It is made out of a metallic foil type material. Your cost on this item is around $9, available from Amazon. Highly recommended.

product_title: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Whole Blueberries 12 oz No. 10 Can
review_text:
Update 6-14-2021 - I had opened the can about 3.5 months ago to do the tests described below. Since then I have been putting them on my cereal occasionally. I had seen in others reviews and the Q&A section that the berries could last up to a year after opening. However, I noticed that by 3 months, the remaining berries, about a 1/4 of the berries, were sticking together and felt slightly gummy. I suspect moisture was getting into the can whenever I opened it. The berries don’t seem to have spoiled, but I doubt the remaining ones would be good several months from now. An identical situation occurred with a can of strawberries. They are no longer crisp as they were when new. In my opinion, these freeze-dried berries need to be consumed within a couple of months of opening.

First, and most important, the weight of the blueberries I received was 12.1 oz, just a hair over the specified weight. So, I got what I paid for. By the way, the unopened can weighs 21 oz. By itself, the can and lid weighs 8.9 oz. So, in the future, I can tell whether I got the correct 12 oz. without having to open the can.

And the can was nearly full, surprising me. About 5.5" of the 7" tall can, or 78%, was full of berries.

Second is the number of servings. Following the printed statement on the can label, I measured out 13 grams, or 1/2 cup, of berries that was supposed to equal one serving. 13 grams did equal 1/2 cup. I actually got 25-1/3 servings from the 12.1 ounces of berries. So, the difference in the 2/3 "missing" serving could be due to one or two extra berries in many of the other cups full. I won't quibble over the slight "shortage," especially since I got the specified 12 ounces.

Third, the quality. The berries tasted good. Both dry and rehydrated, they had a reasonably sweet taste, just a little tart as you might expect from blueberries. The taste was slightly different from some fresh blueberries I have. The main difference is that when dry, they are very crunchy. When rehydrated, they are squishy. They do not have the firmness of fresh berries. But that should be expected.

As for their appearance, they are shriveled as expected, but they were good-sized even when dry (see pictures). The coloring was the expected "blue" color of blueberries. Some had white areas on them, but when I loooked closely, these were where the outer skin and peeled off. I don't think there is anything wrong with them.

Finally, I rehydrated some, following the directions on the label (1/2 cup of berries in 1 cup of warm water). I left them in the water for about 15 minutes to make sure they were rehydrated as much as possible. One thing I noticed was that only about 1/4 of the 1 cup of water was absorbed. There was about 3/4 cup of blueberry water left over.

In the Q&A section, one person estimated that the rehydrated berries would be equal to 6.5 pints (2 cups to a pint - 26 servings/4 = 6.5). The rehydrated berries were actually about the same 1/2 cup in volume as the dried berries.  Four 1/2 cups of the rehydrated berries would probably be almost a pint in volume. In terms of numbers of berries, you might get about the similar numbers. I counted 36 fresh berries into a 1/2 cup and 45 dry berries into the same 1/2 cup. The rehydrated berries weighed about 2 oz while a matching 1/2 cup of fresh berries weighed 2.5 oz.

Rehydration is not required. They can be eaten straight from the can - if you have a taste for blueberries. I would add them to my cereal, where I have blueberries most days.

Next is the cost. These berries cost $33.65 or $2.80/ounce. But if we assume that the 12 ounces of berries were roughly equivalent to, let's say, 6 pints, then the cost per pint is $5.61/pint. But I bought a pint of fresh blueberries the other day for $3.29. Rarely do I pay more than $3.50 for a pint. I have paid as little as $2.50 a pint from a store.

Also, for comparison, I bought two different kinds of dried blueberries at an "organic" food store. One carton cost $1.66/ounce while a bag was $.73/ounce. The two packages had 14 ounces and cost a combined $14.88. So, if you can find them, you can get dried blueberries a lot cheaper at a local store. But the "best by" dates are only a few months away. So, they are for current use, not long-term storage.

So, we pay the extra cost for the benefit of being able to store the blueberries for an extended period of time - for emergencies. And I would buy these again for such a contingency. (Now that I've opened the can, I will need to eat them in the next few months.) But I would NOT buy these for regular or daily use if I had access to dried berries at the grocery store.

Oh, handling the dried blueberries may turn your fingers blue.

PS: Some people think that because they get a large can, they should get it full of berries. But the picture clearly shows that the net weight is 12 oz. (or is supposed to be). I'm not sure why they chose 12 oz., but a check of other vendors shows that they also put only 10-13 ounces of berries in their containers. Yes, Augason could put more berries in the can, but they would charge more for the berries. There is a cost associated with the production - the more berries, the higher the cost. (I've picked blueberries, so I know how long it can take.) The #10 can is a standard sized can used not only by Augason, but also other manufacturers who sell long-shelf-life food products. Using one size can is cheaper than having many different size cans. I have #10 cans with products weighing 2+ pounds. So, 12 ounces might fill only part of the can. In my case, it was most of the can. If someone got only 1/2 to 2/3 of a can full, then they might question the amount. But you have to go by weight, not apparent volume.
pain_point: berries stick together and become gummy after 3 months of opening

product_title: Camco TST MAX RV Toilet Treatment Singles | Features an Ultra-concentrated Biodegradable Septic Safe Formula, an Orange Scent, and is Ideal for RVing, Boating, and More | (8) 4 oz Bottles (41191)
review_text:
I started living in an RV nearly 4 months now no noisy neighbors 5 inches away now.

At first I started using some drop in packets made by Thetford just because the packets were easier even though the packets cost about 70 cents each.

I found this orange scented TST and decided to switch to this instead of the packets because a treatment of liquid TST is only 31 cents, and I can get it locally.

A lot of people do not like to use liquids for one reason or another. The TST Is plentiful and the packets are often sold out.

Using luquid TST could not be easier. 2 fl OZs (60 ml) of TST treats a 40 gallon black water tank. 2 fl OZs is 1/4th a cup so get a 1/4 cup measuring cup and keep it with the TST.

What I did was take one of the many scoops that came in Whey protein (most of the protein scoops are 65 cc scoops. Now 65 cc is the same as 65 ml so I took one of these 65 cc scoops and cut the handle off and turned upside down over the lid of the TST.

Before you do the same check the size of the scoop (usually printed on the bottom of the scoop) a few whey protein scoops are larger because of sugar and flavorings.

First I dump the black water tank, then I fill the scoop almost full and pour it in the commode, and release it into the black water tank with the necessary amount of water. There is always a drop or three staying inside the scoop.

Since the same product can be used to treat the grey water too I rinse the scoop with water at the vanity and then I return the scoop upside down over the lid of the TST.

If I was bookdocking I would put a full treatment of TST in the grey water but while parked at an RV court with the grey water tank open; this is not mecessary unless the grey water tank starts to smell.

Now the last two things.

1. The TST works better than the packets I was using. I am very glad I switched. With the TST there is 0 odor.

2. In another TST product I saw a 1 star review where the person dumped the black water tank three days after treating the black water tank with TST.

That reviewer did a big NO NO. he switched to TST from another treatment without dumping and then flushing the black water tank with water to completely remove the previous chemical. Any time you have two different chemicals in the tank there will be bad odors.

I brought this up so others will know how and why it happened. TST is a great product.
